title: Turkey, Iraq and KRG Finalize Handover Points for PKK Disarmament in Northern Iraq
detail: Officials from Turkey's National Intelligence Organization (MİT), Iraq's National Security Service and the Kurdistan Region Security Council met in Erbil to finalize a mechanism for roughly 4,200 PKK members to lay down arms and vacate 18 camps, positions and caves in northern Iraq — spanning Amedi, Kani Masi, Zakho, Avashin, Said Sadiq, Ranya, Dukan, Koya, Mount Korek and Sidakan — as the next phase of the 'Peace and Democratic Society Process' framework law passed in August. Five handover points are planned around Erbil and Sulaymaniyah, with additional points in Duhok, though the parties had yet to agree who would take physical custody of the surrendered weapons. Positions on Mount Qandil, where the PKK's main command is based, are not part of this first stage. The first phase was expected to begin within days and take about a month, ahead of an October 1 target for confirming the group's disbandment to Turkey's National Security Council.
confidenceReason: Based on officials' plans as reported by regional outlets; final custody arrangements for surrendered weapons were not yet agreed at time of reporting.

title: Police, Gendarmerie Reviewed 600,000+ Social Media Accounts in 2025, Annual Reports Show
detail: Annual activity reports from Turkey's National Police Department and Gendarmerie General Command showed the two forces reviewed a combined 600,180 social media accounts in 2025 under 'virtual/online patrol' programs — up roughly 60% from 374,030 in 2024 — and opened proceedings against 210,234 identified users (up ~72% year-on-year), including 8,471 detentions, 496 arrests and 1,360 placed under judicial supervision. Monitored content included alleged terrorist propaganda, drug promotion, incitement to hatred, and posts deemed insulting to President Erdoğan, the Turkish nation, state institutions, or Atatürk. Press-freedom monitors noted the practice continues despite a 2020 Constitutional Court ruling that struck down the legal provision authorizing online-patrol surveillance as a violation of personal-data and democratic-rights protections.

media.caption: Turkish police and gendarmerie reported reviewing over 600,000 social media accounts in 2025
